claims.claim_text: The pinned repository is a long-lived, multi-channel agent runtime; the bounded case follows one Telegram direct-message path through durable ingress, routing/session state, OpenClaw's embedded-agent runtime, and Telegram delivery rather than treating every bundled integration as ordinary behavior.
claims.confidence: high for the pin and traced path; other channels, hosted services, ACP, Codex, and alternate harness plugins are outside the deep boundary

claims.claim_text: The representative polling path uses isolated ingress by default, a SQLite-backed deduplicating queue, lane-scoped draining, centralized authorization before cache/dedupe mutation, and retry or dead-letter handling before an update reaches the agent dispatcher.
claims.artifact_location: Durable Telegram ingress before the model
claims.confidence: high for admitted text DMs in polling mode; webhook, group/topic, media, and non-default policy branches differ

claims.claim_text: Telegram labels its receive-acknowledgement policy after_agent_dispatch, but the implementation acknowledges that stage when the bot middleware chain returns successfully. Near-limit text and media-group handlers can return after placing admitted content only in process-local timer buffers, after which polling deletes the claimed spool record; a process failure before timer-driven dispatch can therefore lose those buffered updates.
claims.confidence: moderate; the acknowledgement mapping and buffer/spool sequence are directly observed, but no crash reproduction, incidence measurement, or cross-branch behavioral test was performed

references.location: extensions/telegram/src/bot-core.ts:191-221; bot-update-tracker.ts:163-181,232-258; bot-update-tracker.test.ts:78-114; bot-handlers.runtime.ts:803-960,1125-1150,1695-1821; polling-session.ts:521-545
references.notes: Primary verified that bot-core configures after_agent_dispatch but calls finishUpdate(completed:true) on middleware-chain return; the tracker maps that completion to the agent_dispatch acknowledgement stage; buffered handlers return before timer-driven processing and actual reply-chain dispatch; polling then deletes the claimed spool. The tracker unit test covers finishUpdate semantics but not this buffered composition, so the crash consequence remains an explicit inference.

claims.claim_text: Routing and session identity are separate from channel delivery identity: an ordinary default-account direct message resolves through sender-aware routing but, with the default dmScope, normally uses the shared agent:main:main session; named-account fallback and explicit bindings can isolate it.
claims.artifact_location: Routing is not the same as session isolation
claims.confidence: high for the stated configuration; deployments can select peer-scoped sessions, topics, agents, or bindings

claims.confidence: high for mechanics; which layer dominates depends on channel, session sharing, and queue configuration
